Prior-round scores and feedback surface directly above the rubric so reviewers can calibrate their scores without switching views. After a round closes, the portal stays accessible in read-only mode so reviewers can reference their work without accidentally submitting changes.

entries.title: Ask gains session transcripts, action proposals, thumbs feedback and organizer handoff
entries.summary: The **Ask** AI assistant in the attendee app adds four capabilities. **Session transcripts**: Ask can now read live captions and recorded transcripts to answer questions like "what did the speaker say about X?" with cited passage cards. **Action proposals**: Ask can propose adding a session to your schedule (with gap and clash analysis), opening a location on the map, sending a meeting request, or messaging a team — each offered only when the relevant feature is enabled. **Feedback**: attendees can rate any Ask answer with a thumbs up or down. **Handoff to organizer**: attendees can escalate an unanswered question to the organizing team; the reply arrives in the attendee's messaging inbox and organizers respond from their **Messages** inbox. The **Ask** settings panel now shows `feedback` and `handoff` as toggleable features, and admin stats include feedback ratings and handoff counts.

where.path: Attend → Ask (attendee app) and Attend → Ask → Settings (admin)

entries.use_case: Attendees who missed part of a session can ask Ask what was covered and get cited transcript passages. When they have a question the AI cannot resolve, they can hand it off to the organizer team and receive a reply in-app — reducing support load on event staff while keeping attendees informed.

cs_action.note: Transcript access, action proposals (map, meetings, messaging) and handoff routing each depend on separate feature flags being active. Confirm the event has live captions or recorded transcripts, networking/meetings enabled, and a published map before demoing those capabilities.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer asks how attendees can get more value from session content after the fact, or when they want to reduce the volume of 'where is X?' and 'what did the speaker say about Y?' questions to event staff.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers already using the Attend app (beta) who also have Live Transcribe or recorded transcripts, and who want a self-serve attendee support loop.
internal.staff_path: Event → Attend → Ask → Settings
internal.gotchas: Action proposals are gated: map proposals require a published map; meeting/messaging proposals require networking to be on. Handoff creates one organizer thread per attendee registration and is idempotent per answer — a second tap on the same answer will not open a duplicate thread. Transcript passages are capped at 240 characters per citation.
internal.talk_track: Attendees can now ask Ask 'what did the keynote say about AI regulation?' and get a cited excerpt from the live transcript. If Ask can't answer, they tap Escalate and the question lands in your Messages inbox — you reply there and they get a push notification.

draft.docs_gap: The /attend/ask guide should document the new transcript citation card format, the four action proposal types and their feature prerequisites, the feedback (thumbs) UI, the handoff flow for both attendees and organizers, and the new feedback/handoff toggles in Ask Settings.
draft.why_use_it: Ask lets attendees get instant, event-aware answers without hunting through the agenda or flagging down staff. It reads the live programme, session transcripts, the venue map and the attendee's personal schedule to give specific, cited answers. When Ask cannot help, attendees can rate the response or escalate directly to the organizing team and receive a reply in their messaging inbox.

entries.title: Attend app tracks attendee location through check-ins, booth scans and partner zone mappings
entries.summary: Room check-ins, check-outs and exhibitor lead scans now write a presence signal that the app's AI assistant (**Ask**) uses to answer "near me" questions. Organizers can map third-party location provider zones (CrowdConnected, FieldDrive, xTag) to rooms, booths or venue-map pins under **Attend → Location → Zones**, and **Ask** resolves an attendee's current location from the freshest signal — partner or device reads count for 10 minutes, check-ins and booth scans for 30 — before falling back to a session happening now on their schedule. Presence data is automatically purged after 30 days.
entries.use_case: Events using hardware location providers (CrowdConnected, FieldDrive, xTag) or standard room QR check-in can now give attendees accurate "near me" answers in Ask without any manual input. Organizers map provider zones once, and the app automatically surfaces relevant sessions, exhibitors and content based on where each attendee actually is.

cs_action.note: Zone mapping admin endpoints are live but there is no documented UI surface yet; confirm with the product team before walking a customer through setup.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer asks how Ask knows where an attendee is, or when they are evaluating a hardware location partner (CrowdConnected, FieldDrive, xTag) alongside Attend.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers running Attend (beta) who use room QR check-in, exhibitor lead retrieval, or a supported hardware location provider and want Ask to give location-aware answers.
internal.staff_path: Attend → Location → Zones (admin API; confirm UI availability with product)
internal.gotchas: Presence signals are written asynchronously after commit and never block the check-in or lead-scan response. A zone with no mapping is stored as type 'zone' and will not resolve to a corpus pin, so Ask falls through to the schedule step. Door check-in (venue entry) does NOT write a presence signal — only room and booth events do. Booth scans are recorded as 'tap' and do not affect session fill or speaker ratings.
internal.talk_track: When an attendee asks Ask 'what's near me?', the app now checks where they actually are — their last room check-in, a booth scan, or a live signal from your location hardware — and answers based on that. You map your provider's zones to rooms and booths once, and everything stays in sync automatically.

draft.docs_gap: The Ask guide should document the location layer: how presence signals are generated (check-in, booth scan, partner zones), the resolution order Ask uses (explicit near → freshest signal → current schedule session), the signal expiry windows (10 min for partner/device/map, 30 min for check-in/booth scan), how to set up zone mappings under Attend → Location → Zones, and the 30-day automatic retention policy.
draft.why_use_it: Ask uses the attendee's current location — derived from check-ins, booth scans or a connected hardware provider — to answer questions like "what's happening near me?" or "which exhibitors are close by?" without the attendee having to say where they are. You can map zones from any supported location partner to the same rooms, booths and pins the rest of the app uses, so every feature stays in sync. Presence signals respect the attendee's consent settings and are automatically cleaned up after 30 days.

entries.title: Advocacy notify dialog lets you email only new campaign recipients
entries.summary: When sending notifications on a campaign that has already been emailed, the **Notify** dialog now offers two choices: **Everyone (N)** to re-send to all recipients, or **Only new (M)** to reach only people added since the last send. The counts come from a live dry run so you always know exactly how many people will receive the message before you confirm.
entries.use_case: Campaigns that grow over time — such as rolling attendee invitations — previously required organizers to manually track who had already been notified to avoid duplicate emails. The **Only new** option lets organizers safely re-open the notify dialog at any point and send only to people who haven't received the campaign email yet.

cs_action.note: Requires the companion API change in lennd/sessionboard-web-api#4584. Until that API ships, the dry-run call returns a 400, the Only new option stays hidden, and Notify behaves as before — no customer impact during the gap.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer running a rolling Advocacy campaign asks how to avoid re-emailing people who already received a campaign notification.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any customer using Advocacy campaigns where recipients are added in batches over time.
internal.staff_path: Event → Marketing → Advocacy → [campaign] → Notify
internal.gotchas: The Only new option is hidden until the API (web-api#4584) is deployed. Deploy order is safe — no regression if the UI ships first.
internal.talk_track: Once your campaign has been sent, the Notify dialog will show you two options: resend to everyone, or reach only the people added since your last send — with exact counts so you know what you're about to do.

draft.docs_gap: The Advocacy guide should document the Everyone / Only new choice in the Notify dialog, including how the dry-run counts work and when the option appears (only after at least one prior send).
draft.why_use_it: Advocacy lets you turn speakers, sponsors, and attendees into a distributed marketing channel by giving each person a personalised sharing link for your event. You can launch a campaign once and keep adding recipients as registrations grow, then notify each new cohort without re-emailing people who already received the message. The live recipient count in the notify dialog shows exactly how many people will be reached before you send.
